questions.text: Why was swapping things confusing in the Barter Days?
options: Nobody could agree on what things were worth
questions.explanation: Swapping was confusing because nobody could agree on the value of things — one cow might be worth ten sheep to one farmer, but only five sheep to another. That is why people invented money: a token everyone agrees has the same value.
False! Swapping was confusing because nobody could agree on value — one cow might be worth ten sheep to one farmer, but only five sheep to another.
questions.text: True or false: in the Barter Days, everybody always agreed on the value of things.
